deck_name: 17 - ARM Cortex-M Registers, Bitwise & Bare-Metal C

cards.prompt: In the ARM Cortex-M core register set (R0–R15), which three special registers correspond to R13, R14, and R15?
cards.answer: R13 = SP (Stack Pointer), R14 = LR (Link Register), R15 = PC (Program Counter)
accepted_answers: Stack Pointer, Link Register, Program Counter
cards.explanation: R13 is SP (MSP/PSP), R14 is LR (holds return address on BL/interrupt entry), and R15 is PC.

cards.prompt: What are the first two 32-bit words stored at the base of the ARM Cortex-M Vector Table (0x0800_0000 on STM32)?
cards.answer: Initial Main Stack Pointer (MSP) value and Reset_Handler address
cards.explanation: On hardware reset, the Cortex-M core loads word 0 into MSP and jumps to the address in word 1 (Reset_Handler).

cards.prompt: Which registers are automatically pushed onto the stack by ARM Cortex-M hardware upon entering an Interrupt Service Routine (ISR)?
cards.answer: R0, R1, R2, R3, R12, LR, PC, xPSR
accepted_answers: xPSR, PC, LR, R12, R3, R2, R1, R0
cards.explanation: Hardware stacking of these 8 caller-saved registers allows standard C functions to serve as ISRs without assembly wrappers.

cards.prompt: Write the standard C bitwise expression to SET bit `n` in a 32-bit hardware register `REG` without altering other bits.
cards.explanation: Using unsigned 1U avoids undefined behavior when shifting into bit 31 (the sign bit of a 32-bit signed int).

cards.prompt: Write the standard C bitwise expression to CLEAR bit `n` in a 32-bit hardware register `REG` without altering other bits.
cards.explanation: ~(1U << n) creates a mask with 0 at bit n and 1s everywhere else; bitwise AND clears only bit n.

cards.prompt: Write the standard C bitwise expression to TOGGLE bit `n` in a 32-bit hardware register `REG`.
cards.explanation: Bitwise XOR flips bit n while preserving every bit masked with 0.

cards.prompt: Why must pointers to Memory-Mapped I/O (MMIO) registers and variables shared with ISRs be qualified with `volatile` in C?
cards.answer: To prevent the compiler from caching the value in a CPU register or optimizing away repeated reads/writes
accepted_answers: Force every read and write to hit memory
cards.explanation: volatile tells the compiler the value can change asynchronously outside normal program flow (by hardware or an ISR).

cards.prompt: Does `volatile` alone guarantee atomic read-modify-write operations or thread synchronization across interrupts?
accepted_answers: No. Use critical sections or atomics
cards.explanation: A read-modify-write like `REG |= (1U << 3)` compiles to LDR, ORR, STR; an ISR firing mid-sequence can cause a lost update unless protected.

cards.prompt: Why do STM32 GPIO peripherals provide a dedicated BSRR (Bit Set/Reset Register) in addition to ODR (Output Data Register)?
cards.answer: BSRR performs atomic single-cycle pin set/reset writes without a read-modify-write race condition
cards.explanation: Writing 1 to the lower 16 bits of BSRR sets pins and writing 1 to the upper 16 bits resets pins atomically (0 bits are ignored).

cards.prompt: In an embedded C executable, what is the difference between the `.data` section and the `.bss` section?
cards.answer: .data holds initialized global/static variables (copied from Flash to RAM at startup); .bss holds zero-initialized globals/statics (zeroed in RAM at startup)
accepted_answers: .data is initialized non-zero globals, .bss is zero-initialized globals
cards.explanation: .bss consumes zero Flash storage for initial values—only its start and end addresses are stored so Reset_Handler can zero-fill it.

cards.prompt: In which memory region and section are `const` lookup tables and string literals stored on an ARM Cortex-M microcontroller?
cards.explanation: Placing constant tables in .rodata keeps them in non-volatile Flash rather than consuming scarce SRAM.

cards.prompt: In the ARM Cortex-M NVIC, does a lower numerical priority value (e.g., 0) represent higher or lower interrupt urgency than priority 5?
cards.explanation: On ARM Cortex-M, lower priority numbers have higher urgency; priority 0 is the highest configurable interrupt priority.

cards.prompt: What built-in 24-bit downward-counting timer inside every ARM Cortex-M core is typically used to generate a 1 ms system tick?
cards.explanation: SysTick is part of the Cortex-M System Control Space (SCS), making 1 ms tick drivers portable across all Cortex-M vendors.

cards.prompt: Predict the exact hex output (formatted as 0xXXXX):
cards.explanation: Masking with ~0x00F0 clears bits [7:4] (yielding 0x1204), and ORing with 0x00A0 inserts 0xA into that nibble -> 0x12A4.

cards.prompt: On ARM Cortex-M, what exception is triggered by an invalid memory access, unaligned access, or stack overflow when configurable faults are disabled?
cards.explanation: HardFault (priority -1) is the catch-all fault handler; inspecting SCB->CFSR and the stacked PC reveals the faulting instruction.

cards.prompt: Why do I2C SDA and SCL lines require external or internal pull-up resistors?
cards.answer: Because I2C uses open-drain drivers that can only pull the bus LOW, relying on pull-ups to return the line HIGH
accepted_answers: Devices only drive LOW; pull-ups bring the line HIGH
cards.explanation: Open-drain signaling prevents bus contention when multiple devices share SDA/SCL and enables clock stretching and arbitration.

cards.prompt: In SPI communication, what do CPOL and CPHA configure?
cards.answer: Clock Polarity (idle clock level) and Clock Phase (which clock edge samples/shifts data)
cards.explanation: CPOL (0 or 1) and CPHA (0 or 1) combine to define SPI Modes 0, 1, 2, and 3.

cards.prompt: In a Single-Producer Single-Consumer (SPSC) lock-free ring buffer (e.g., UART RX ISR -> main loop), why is no mutex required?
cards.answer: Only the producer updates the head/write index and only the consumer updates the tail/read index
accepted_answers: Producer owns write index, consumer owns read index
cards.explanation: With power-of-two capacity and proper memory barriers/atomics, disjoint index ownership prevents concurrent writes to the same variable.

cards.prompt: In Q16.16 fixed-point arithmetic (1.0 == 65536 == 0x00010000), what integer value represents 2.5?
cards.explanation: 2.5 * 65536 = 163840 (0x00028000), allowing fast deterministic integer math on MCUs without an FPU.

cards.prompt: Why does the Thumb-2 instruction set on ARM Cortex-M require the least significant bit (LSB, bit 0) of every function address in the Vector Table to be 1?
cards.answer: Bit 0 indicates Thumb execution state; clearing bit 0 causes an INVSTATE UsageFault/HardFault
cards.explanation: Cortex-M cores only execute Thumb/Thumb-2 instructions; the `.thumb_func` assembler directive automatically sets bit 0 on handler labels.
